value: Fig. 7 panel g — gate discrimination: per-session distributions of the gate score for imagined walking vs resting control on one shared decision boundary, plus the per-trial accuracy at that boundary. figures_out/fig7/main/fig7_gate_discrimination.png + _legend.png. No in-figure title, no in-panel statistics block.

post_operative, n = 2 patients, case-level (11 sessions: pat01_sess04, pat01_sess05, pat01_sess06, pat01_sess07, pat01_sess08, pat01_sess09, pat02_sess03, pat02_sess05, pat02_sess06, pat02_sess08, pat02_sess09). The gate uses 11 of 11 sessions. Eleven sessions from two people is not a population estimate.

e_sigma — the fused score (fuse_V1) standardised by the (theta_sym, delta) of the fold that emitted it: e_sigma = (fuse_V1 - theta_sym) / delta. The decision boundary is therefore 0 for EVERY row of EVERY session and one dotted line at 0 serves all 12 rows; in RAW units each of the 10 folds has its own theta_sym, so no single raw boundary exists. The pooled row is the union of the standardised decisions of all 11 sessions (2,605), not a mean of session distributions.

theta_sym is the two conditions' natural zero computed from each fold's TRAINING folds — ((0 - centre_A)/sd_A + (0 - centre_B)/sd_B)/2 — and is never fitted to the scored windows. The accuracy reported here is therefore accuracy at a pre-specified operating point, not at a threshold chosen on the data being scored.

1.0 delta units, FIXED for every row and both classes (gaussian_kde with bw_method = 1.0 / std(x)), so the smoothing is identical across sessions and rows are comparable. Evaluated on 400 points from -20 to 30 delta units (row_type=density is exactly the plotted curve). The KDE is fitted to the unclipped data; mass beyond the axis is off-axis, not piled up at the edge.
row_type=box — box 25-75 %, whiskers 10-90 %, median; computed on all decisions of that row and class (no outlier markers).

Per-trial accuracy at the symmetric boundary. For each evaluated trial (event) the fraction of its 1 s-hop decisions on its own side of theta_sym (correct iff (e_sigma >= 0) == (label == 1); no decision has e_sigma exactly 0, asserted at run time). The dot is the MEAN OVER TRIALS of that fraction, so every trial weighs the same regardless of its duration; the capped bar is a percentile (2.5 / 97.5) bootstrap OVER TRIALS, B = 1000, seed 0, each row drawn from its own np.random.default_rng(0). This is NOT the decision-weighted accuracy: row_type=accuracy carries both, decision_level_accuracy being the S0 accuracy of 03_figures/fig7_gate_accuracy_table.py (asserted equal to 1e-6 at run time).
The continuous vertical line through the right column is the pooled mean trial accuracy (the POOLED row's dot), drawn once in figure coordinates.

Fig. 6d rule — light = fill (hue at COND_FILL_ALPHA = 0.32 on white), dark = edge (the hue itself). Imagined walking = IW_HUE #2E6E5E, resting control = REST_HUE #BA7517 (03_figures/project_palette.py). Hue encodes the CONDITION only; no hue carries a verdict. Decision boundary and accuracy marker in INK #1A1A1A; pooled guide in MID #666666.
